item.title: Inappropriate Antibiotic Use for COVID-19 Is Linked to Resistance
item.description: Azithromycin was used early in the pandemic to treat COVID-19 in patients and has continued to be used to fight respiratory illnesses. But a new UCSF-led study supports findings that show it isn't effective and that it has negative consequences.

item.title: UCSF Researcher Earns Top Honors at Orthopaedic Surgery Conference
item.description: The American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons (AAOS) has awarded the 2026 New Emerging eXperts in Translational Science (NEXT) Award to Kelsey H. Collins, PhD, for her research on the role that fat tissue plays as a key contributor to osteoarthritis (OA).

item.title: This Multiview AI Imaging Can Improve Cardiac Diagnostic Accuracy
item.description: Heart disease is the leading cause of adult death worldwide, making cardiovascular disease diagnosis and management a global health priority. An echocardiogram, or cardiac ultrasound, is one of the most commonly used imaging tools employed by physicians to diagnose a variety of heart diseases and conditions.

item.title: Scientists Create Cancer-Fighting Immune Cells Right in the Body
item.description: UCSF scientists found a precise way to turn on cancer-fighting immune cells inside the body. This more potent form of CAR-T has the potential to treat many more cancers.

item.title: UCSF’s New Certification Raises Bar for Spine Surgery Excellence
item.description: UCSF’s neurological surgery and orthopaedic surgery departments have earned the Joint Commission’s Advanced Certification in Spine Surgery. UCSF Health is one of only five hospitals in California to achieve this national certification.

item.title: Haven’t Heard of Lynch Syndrome? You’re Not Alone.
item.description: The UCSF Lynch Syndrome Center is a leading Northern California clinic specializing in Lynch syndrome, a common genetic condition increasing the risk of colon cancer and other cancers. The center offers comprehensive, multidisciplinary care, advanced cancer screening, and cutting-edge treatments, including an NIH-funded vaccine trial, to nearly 1,000 patients.

item.title: Brian Smith to Retire as Chief Ethics and Compliance Officer
item.description: Brian Smith, UCSF’s ethics chief, will retire on August 1 after 11 years, leaving a legacy of institutional integrity and oversight across the university’s expansive research and clinical operations.

item.title: Michael Bishop, Nobel-Winning Cancer Researcher, Has Died at 90
item.description: Former UCSF Chancellor and Nobel-Prize winning cancer researcher, J. Michael Bishop, has died at the age of 90.

item.title: Are Psychedelics Better than Antidepressants? New Study Says No
item.description: New research pits psychedelic-assisted therapy against traditional antidepressants in an unblinded study that presents a sobering viewpoint on the treatment's potential.

item.title: Is Your Brain Aging Faster Than You Are? Sleep May Hold the Key
item.description: Poor sleep is associated with an increased risk for dementia, but many sleep studies have had inconsistent results. For the first time, used AI to analyze tiny electrical signals in the brain of 7,000 participants healthy participants to calculate “brain age." They find that dementia risk increases significantly when the brain age exceeds actual age.
